_about: Side-by-side mode: the numbers for what MORDHAU's character sets down or throws once it exists in Skyrim's world (models: sheets/props.json; keys: sheets/live_input.json). Distances in Skyrim units unless the id says cm; MORDHAU damage values are of its 100 health and go through sheets/progression.json like any MORDHAU-judged hit. source says where each number is from.

rows.meaning: MORDHAU's world gravity, cm/s^2 (Unreal's default)
Skyrim's stealth eye while MORDHAU is linked: moved this far left of the screen's middle (HUD units, 1280 wide)
... and this far down (HUD units, 720 high)
how near (Skyrim units) the player must stand to the dropped weapon for E to pick it up

Skyrim's fCombatDistance while MORDHAU is linked (Skyrim's own: 141 units = 201 cm, farther than MORDHAU blades reach: enemies swung short of the player). 90 units x the weapon's reach = 129 cm for a sword, 167 cm for a greatsword. Put back when the link ends.
rows.source: measured from the swing log 2026-10-07: swings started from 190-330 cm

rows.meaning: seconds into the release before Skyrim's world can stop the player's blade (MORDHAU has a curve for this, FC_StrikeWorldCollisionPercentage: a swing that starts beside a wall is not stopped at once)
only this outer share of the blade is tested against Skyrim's world (the hands and the lower blade pass close to things all the time)
0 = OFF (play-test note, 2026-10-08). Otherwise: how far (Skyrim units) the player's surroundings are felt for walls, in three directions at chest height
1 = the plugin itself also ends an attack whose blade meets Skyrim's world (no recoil); 0 = left to MORDHAU, which meets the unseen wall piece and recoils by its own rules

play-test note, 2026-10-15: 'npcs are hitting invisible objects'. 0 = no attack in the mod's session is stopped by MORDHAU's own map (its walls, pillars and props stand where they stand in MORDHAU's arena, not where Skyrim's are): the script sets MORDHAU's bDisableWorldCollision on every attack motion, the player's and the stand-ins'. In the D: test before: 21 enemy swings thrown back (BlockedMotion) 4-6 m from the player, who was not parrying. Skyrim's walls do not stop a blade either while wall_reach and wall_cut are 0 (both off since the play tests of 2026-10-08) - before this, only MORDHAU's map did, at places that had nothing to do with Skyrim's. Script: main.lua PS_no_world_hits (always on; this row is its note).
rows.source: the D: test log, 2026-10-15; MORDHAU's attack motion property found by listing BP_1H_RightStrikeMotion's properties

rows.meaning: 1 = the player's weapon is drawn as the Skyrim weapon that is equipped (Skyrim's own model and textures, placed where MORDHAU's counterpart is); 0 = MORDHAU's model. A weapon picked up in MORDHAU that is not the equipped one's counterpart is always MORDHAU's model.

1 = people are Skyrim's own models (their real armour, faces, weapons) moved by MORDHAU's skeleton: whoever is fought - and the player in third person - has the Skyrim skeleton posed from MORDHAU's pose each frame (the bone map of sheets/bone_map.json, run backwards); nobody is drawn as a MORDHAU body. 0 = MORDHAU bodies in MORDHAU armour, as before. A test key overrides it: skyrimbodies=1 in the dev file.
how far above the spot (Skyrim units) the Skyrim copy of a dropped weapon is set down, to fall the rest by Skyrim's physics (at 12 it started inside the ground and fell through)

an enemy that already has a MORDHAU stand-in counts as this much nearer (Skyrim units) when the three nearest fighters are chosen, so stand-ins are not swapped back and forth between enemies at about the same distance

while an ENB is installed (d3d11.dll and enbseries.ini in Skyrim's folder): brightness of everything this plugin draws itself (MORDHAU's first-person body and hands, the weapon in hand, props, gore). A free stand-in is in MORDHAU's movement mode 5 ('flying': it goes where its brain sends it but does not fall) and its HEIGHT is set every frame to what Skyrim has it at against the player - walking on MORDHAU's uneven arena floor it stood 20-38 cm lower than the player (measured 2026-10-09), so chest-high swings passed over it or counted as head hits.

The preview can only show a model file: the plugin writes one per MORDHAU weapon on the player's PC (Data\meshes\MordhauSkyrim, textures in Data	extures\MordhauSkyrim) from the model it has already prepared in its cache out of the player's own MORDHAU - nothing of it is in the download - and puts it in place of the borrowed model once the preview has loaded that one, at its place and size. play-test note, 2026-10-12 (people on level ground kept starting Skyrim's falling animation): a fought character counts as having yielded - its body is Skyrim's alone, see fought_no_retreat - only after Skyrim has had it out of combat for this long without a break. Skyrim drops and retakes its combat state for moments during a fight; each time the body went to Skyrim's own animation while MORDHAU's AI was still walking it, and a body moved that way is 'falling' to Skyrim. Fleeing and kneeling still count at once. And while a body is Skyrim's alone, MORDHAU's AI does not walk it.

play-test note and a Nexus comment, 2026-10-13: fought characters move in small jerks. Recorded frame by frame: a stand-in walking evenly is reported in uneven steps (0.6 to 4.5 units in neighbouring frames with the player standing still) because MORDHAU's frames are of uneven length (11-23 ms) and not in step with Skyrim's, and each report was shown for exactly one Skyrim frame. 1 = every report carries MORDHAU's own game time; the plugin takes the stand-in's speed from two reports and walks the character to where the stand-in is at the MORDHAU time that belongs to the Skyrim frame being drawn (at most hybrid_lead_seconds ahead of the last report); its heading the same way; and its height follows the ground at hybrid_height_rate instead of jumping to it. 0 = as before. (Two earlier tries of the same night did not help and are not in: carrying the last report on by its ARRIVAL times, and easing the angle between the two worlds - which made fighters swing as the view turned.)

play-test note, 2026-10-13 ('seems the jitters mainly happen when i move'; recorded: with the player walking, the place MORDHAU reports for a free stand-in steps back against its own last step in 11-12% of frames, standing still in 1-4%). MORDHAU's player character walks on the spot: it is let stray up to 5 cm and then set back. Where a free stand-in stands in Skyrim's world, and the shift that keeps it there while the player walks and turns, were reckoned from wherever that character was in the frame - so each stand-in's place took on the same 0-5 cm saw-tooth. Now both are reckoned from the fixed spot. A held stand-in is still placed against the character itself.

play-test note, 2026-10-13 (a bandit kicking: 'he tried moving forwards and got teleported back then walked forward again and again teleport'). MORDHAU lets two fighters stand nearer to each other than Skyrim lets two characters: walked to where its stand-in is in a lunge, the character was put into the player, Skyrim pushed it out again (recorded: it moved 1.3 units a frame while its stand-in moved 5.5, 39-48 units from the player), the two came apart and the script set the stand-in back to its character. A walked character is now never put nearer to the player than this; the few centimetres between it and its stand-in are far inside what the script tolerates. 2026-10-13, same day, after 0.1.14-0.1.16 were out: 'whenever an enemy comes close to me he starts teleporting back then runs back to me'. Holding only the Skyrim body off was half of it: MORDHAU's player walks on the spot, so walking into a fighter shifts his stand-in towards that spot without limit, body and stand-in come apart and the script sets the stand-in back. The stand-in is now held off the player's spot at the same distance (the script's PLAYER_GAP, 72 cm). Later the same day (report: 'whenever an enemy comes close to me he starts teleporting back then runs back to me'): the limit that matters is MORDHAU's. Its characters are 50 cm round (CapsuleRadius read in play), so two never stand nearer than 100 cm = 70 units. Walking INTO a fighter in Skyrim shifted his stand-in inside that, MORDHAU threw it back out the next frame (recorded: its place flipping 47 <-> 69 units from the player every frame). The script now holds a free stand-in 101 cm off the player's spot itself (PS_PLAYER_GAP in main.lua). Measured in one session, 45 s each, walking into a bandit: jumps of his place close to the player 29 and 7 with the rule off, 1 and 1 with it on.

play-test note, 2026-10-13 ('i am looking at the top of his head ... a straight horizontal swing goes directly over'). Measured side by side (tools/heights_compare.py, both games logging the same heights with MORDHAU's game time): the feet of a fought character agree between the two games to about a centimetre, but MORDHAU had its head and hips 9-11 cm HIGHER than Skyrim shows them (within 5 cm only 11-20% of the time). Skyrim draws people in their own sizes - a bandit at 0.98, the player at 1.03 - and in MORDHAU the player and every stand-in are one size. 1 = each stand-in is given its Skyrim character's size against the player's (the two scales divided), so a swing meets the body where it is seen. 0 = all one size, as before.

A free stand-in walks MORDHAU's own ground, which is not Skyrim's: its body is raised or lowered against its capsule so that it stands against the player as its Skyrim character does. The most it is shifted. 60 until 2026-10-13; measured then (tools/heights_compare.py, duels in Riverwood and Whiterun): the shift needed was beyond 60 cm in 4-21% of the samples - the arena's steps and ledges - and never beyond 150; in those moments the stand-in stood up to 75 cm away from where Skyrim showed the fighter. The script's BODY_SHIFT_MOST.

play-test note, 2026-10-13: 'i want kicks to stagger non mordhau enemies'. 1 = the player's kick staggers whoever it reaches that has no MORDHAU stand-in (a wolf, a spider, a draugr beyond the stand-in count ...): Skyrim's own stagger, away from the player. Against a stand-in MORDHAU judges the kick itself, as before. A kick no longer counts as a weapon hit on such an enemy: until now the held weapon's blade was tested during the kick's release and gave a full weapon hit where it happened to pass (seen in the log: 'MORDHAU's blade (BP_KickMotion_C) reached Falmer'). Same day, in play: 'you cant combo after, the hit counts as a miss' - MORDHAU knows nothing of an enemy without a stand-in, so its kick ran out as a missed one. The plugin now tells the script (request KickLanded) and the script ends the kick motion there, so the next attack can be started at once; MORDHAU's hit marker and hit sound are given as for any hit Skyrim judges.
how hard that stagger is, as Skyrim counts it (its staggerMagnitude: 0.25 a flinch, 0.5 a step back, 0.75 several steps, 1 the longest)
rows.source: chosen: a clear step back without the longest animation

The player's kick on anyone without a MORDHAU stand-in (a wolf, a skeever, a draugr beyond the stand-in count ...) takes this share of one clean hit (progression.json clean_hit), times creature_damage_scale for creatures - as a weapon hit of that size is judged by Skyrim's progression. 0 = the kick does no damage (stagger, marker and sound only, as before). play-test note, 2026-10-13: 'make it so the alt mode on applicable shields block damage from creatures'. 1 = while MORDHAU's shield wall is up (the shield's alternate mode, MORDHAU's R; streamed back as a ShieldParry motion in its blocking stage 0), a hit Skyrim judges on the player from the front - a creature's bite or claw, an arrow - is stopped, as one is by the timed parry or by the held block button. Until now only the block button counted: the wall raised with R stopped MORDHAU's own fighters but not Skyrim's creatures.

Play-test note 2026-10-14: 'now creatures only take damage in the head' - the stand-in, a person at the creature's front, only met swings at the head. Since then the blade is ALSO tested against the creature's whole body (as before the stand-in), and each swing counts once per creature, whichever test counts it first. play-test note, 2026-10-13: 'is it possible to have a small mordhau character who doesnt attack at the front of the creatures so when you kick ...' - 'make it'. 1 = a creature that fights the player (a wolf, a spider, a skeever: anything that is not a person) gets a MORDHAU stand-in that only stands to be hit: passive (never attacks, never parries), held at the creature's front end, as tall against the player as the creature is. MORDHAU itself then judges whether the player's swing or kick lands on it - so a landed kick is a landed kick, a hit can be followed by a combo, a blunt weapon stops in the body - while the creature stays Skyrim's in everything else: its body, its animation, its movement, its own attacks on the player. The damage is still the creature kind (creature_damage_scale of a clean hit); a landed kick gives Skyrim's stagger (kick_stagger_magnitude) and no damage. Stand-in places left over by people go to the nearest such creatures; one without a stand-in (no place left, or taller than creature_standin_tallest) is judged by the blade against its body as before.

1 = while MORDHAU is linked, True Directional Movement's directional movement and its turning of the player are switched off through TDM's own interface (TDM_API RequestDisableDirectionalMovement / RequestYawControl) and handed back when the link ends. Players running TDM could only walk forward with the weapon put away (Nexus reports, 2026-10-13/14: 'I can only move forward when my weapon is sheathed', 'I cannot walk sideways'): TDM turned the character toward where the player pressed, this mod keeps it facing the view. Since 2026-10-15 also TDM's target lock (its key is the middle mouse button, this mod's cast key - the user: 'middle mouse is tdm lockon feature but also our spellcast, do something about that'), through TDM's own interface (RequestDisableTargetLock), given back with the rest.
